avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Valsartan reduces aldosterone, increasing potassium retention; concurrent supplementation elevates hyperkalemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid potassium supplements unless serum potassium is documented low; monitor K+ levels regularly

avoid_supplements.name: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce antihypertensive efficacy and increase renal dysfunction and hyperkalemia risk with ARBs
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid chronic NSAID use; use acetaminophen for analgesia instead

avoid_supplements.name: ACE inhibitors (lisinopril, enalapril)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Dual blockade of renin-angiotensin system increases hyperkalemia, hypotension, and renal impairment risk
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine; valsartan should replace, not supplement, ACE inhibitors

caution_supplements.name: Licorice root
caution_supplements.mechanism: Licorice causes sodium retention and potassium depletion, potentially counteracting valsartan's antihypertensive effects
caution_supplements.action: Limit licorice intake; monitor blood pressure response

caution_supplements.name: Hawthorn
caution_supplements.mechanism: Hawthorn may have additive hypotensive effects with valsartan
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for excessive hypotension; inform provider of concurrent use

caution_supplements.name: Garlic supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Garlic may have mild blood pressure-lowering effects, potentially additive with valsartan
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure; adjust valsartan dose if needed

avoid_foods.name: High-potassium foods (excessive intake)
avoid_foods.mechanism: High dietary potassium combined with valsartan-induced potassium retention increases hyperkalemia risk
avoid_foods.action: Moderate intake of bananas, spinach, sweet potatoes, tomatoes; follow renal dietitian guidance based on K+ levels

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4, potentially increasing valsartan levels; effect is mild with valsartan
caution_foods.action: Limit grapefruit juice consumption; monitor blood pressure response

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium may reduce antihypertensive efficacy of valsartan
caution_foods.action: Encourage low-sodium diet (<2.3g daily sodium) for optimal BP control

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum potassium, creatinine, and BUN at baseline and 1-2 weeks after initiation or dose changes. Watch for signs of hyperkalemia (weakness, palpitations) and renal dysfunction in patients with CKD, diabetes, or elderly populations.
